cells.tense: You are already the thing itself, and the seeing is happening in you now.
cells.ask: Tell one person exactly what you notice about them, without softening it or explaining.
cells.core:
You're not building a name for yourself. You're just letting through what's already yours, and the letting doesn't cost anything because it isn't aimed anywhere. People can feel the difference between someone putting something on and someone letting something through.

When you talk about what you notice, you move between the wide view and the detail, and it holds together. There's a pull to defend it, or to give it a better story. It doesn't need either. What this can feed next is saying less and trusting that what you saw carries. Let someone be changed by it without you managing the change.
cells.sheetLine: You're showing what was always yours.

cells.tense: You are steering toward a future where they finally get it, and you are ahead of where anyone can meet you.
cells.ask: Let one conversation end where it ends, with no summary from you of what it all means.
cells.core:
You're not just seeing the pattern anymore. You're pushing it into the room before anyone asks. You can feel the way it lands — too fast, too total — and you keep going, sure the right phrasing will finally make it click. Here you mistake the beam leaving you for the source of the beam.

So it starts to blind instead of show. People step back. You push harder, thinking the problem is volume. It isn't. The other side is just being in the room, open, with nothing prepared. Don't chase the next moment. You don't know what's coming, and that's the ground. One conversation where the pattern stays unsaid is enough.
cells.sheetLine: You're blinding them with your own light.

cells.tense: You saw something whole a long time ago, and you are still standing behind a door that already opened.
cells.ask: Say one thing you notice about what's in front of you, out loud, even if it lands wrong.
cells.core:
There was a moment when it all came together — the whole shape, at once. Since then you've kept that clear sight in the dark and called it humility. It isn't. It's fear of what comes back if you name it. So you dim what you already are, and it thins out because you don't let it reach anyone.

What has to return is direction. One clear yes, one clear no, one time you pick this over that and mean it. From there, sight finds its feet again. Nothing gets added. You point what you notice at something and let it land. The next person who asks can receive what you saw, no apology attached.
cells.sheetLine: You saw it and then called it nothing.

cells.tense: The shining is already happening, and you are talking about it as if it were someone else's weather.
cells.ask: When the pattern drops open, note under your breath that this is yours, not a mood passing through.
cells.core:
You walk into a room and the shape drops open — what's true, what people are carrying, how the layers stack — and you treat it like something that arrived from outside. 'It's obvious.' 'Anyone would see that.' They don't. This is yours and you're giving it no one's name.

So there's no rest in it. Some days you call it luck. On the quiet ones you're sure it left for good. Neither is true. The smallest move is to own what you catch as yours in the moment it happens — not later, not with a story, just a quiet claim. Then whatever enters next is met from there, and it stays your life instead of the room's.
cells.sheetLine: You're already shining and calling it just the room.
